grade_evidence: (1) READ at source: Table 110 (p.327) prints the 11 bulk masses the owner uses, exactly, including P 780 g and N 1,800 g, the CI binder and its runner-up. (2) CI half, computed: P binds at 10.70 kg/kg on ICRP 23's own values, with N 1.325x behind. Neither the two-figure rounding (H3) nor any alternative estimate the source prints moves it. That half holds for ICRP 23's Reference Man; it is NARROWED only in that the source's object is a 1975 20-30 y male, which the tree calls 'adult'. (3) Photosphere half, computed: P binds at 1910 over Li at 1753, and the binder flips if Li exceeds 7.629 mg. ICRP 23 does not supply that datum: Li is absent from Table 110, and under the caption's 50 % rule ICRP did not know its concentration over half the body. The 7 mg is Emsley's (tertiary restatement), and the same restatement's fraction column implies 2.17 mg (first audit). On Table 110 alone the photosphere binder is P by 2.93x. So whether P binds there depends on a lithium datum that is not ICRP's and is contested. (4) Carried, not re-read: ICRP says P23 is amended by ICRP 89, and ICRP 110 bulk (P 0.813 %) makes Li and C bind (first audit). (5) Not WRONG: no ICRP 23 value is contradicted by a computation. The 14 differing owner values are attribution discrepancies (Emsley under an ICRP label) and move no binder. The 2.63x is a tree-internal mixing of two P values. (6) Not STANDS: the photosphere binder moves with a datum, Li, that is neither ICRP 23's nor settled.
what_would_change_the_grade: A legible image of ICRP 23 Table 108 (pp.289-324, especially the closing section for elements known in <20 % of the body) or of Chapter 3's lithium entry. If either prints a Reference Man Li figure, or a primary measurement of whole-body Li (with uncertainty) lies wholly below 7.63 mg, the photosphere half would be READ. Then, with the CI half already confirmed, the grade would become NARROWED: it holds for ICRP 23's 1975 Reference Man, a male, not for 'an adult'. A primary Li figure wholly above 7.63 mg would make lithium the photosphere binder for the tree's own payload; that would be recorded, not repaired. Reading ICRP 89's reference-male P (flip threshold 1.021 % at the photosphere; 0.840 % for P to cede to N at CI) would settle whether the later ICRP data move the binder for Reference Man itself. Emsley p.83 itself would settle the 14 non-ICRP values.
